findings.reason: The Task* echo test feeds runAgentTurn a stream that has no echo in it (only todo_list_updated plus a Read pair) and then asserts that no echo comes out, so it would pass whatever the turn engine or the adapter did with a real echo. Its only check on the library, CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_TRACKING_TOOLS containing 'TaskCreate', does not pin the suppression either. The scheduling test at line 3828 has the same problem: no scheduling event is ever fed in, so only the CLAUDE_CODE_SUPPRESSED_HARNESS_TOOLS pin there can fail. If the adapter cannot be driven, pin the library's suppression contract directly (a translator-level export or a constant that says the echo is dropped) rather than asserting that an input which was never sent is absent.

The outputFile 'never read' guard spies on the default export object of node:fs (vi.spyOn(fs, 'readFileSync') and the like). Vitest externalizes node built-ins, so code that uses named ESM imports (import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs', or 'node:fs/promises') binds to the module namespace and goes around these spies. A regression that tails outputFile that way would still pass the test; only the MARKER-absence assertions would catch it, and only if the content reached the stream or the row. The test is fine as it stands but weaker than its title says.
